integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Photorealistic live-action film footage of real actors in an ancient Chinese (Song-dynasty) period drama, with the look of a feature film. The one man in this shot is a short, portly man of fifty, filmed from behind him, in an ancient Chinese Song-dynasty rich landlord's dark gold silk cross-collared robe woven with small round medallions, with long wide sleeves and a black belt, and a small round black cap; the location shown in <Picture 1> is the set, keeping its layout: the big old tree and the dry furrowed fields behind it. Initial composition: On the three small fields of Liuxi at dawn the next morning, on the grassy bank under the big old tree, the dry cracked fields of the drought spreading beyond it; soft grey-gold dawn light, a thin white mist lying low over the ground: medium-wide shot from behind him on the grassy bank, framed from the knees up with clear space above his cap: the portly man stands left of the middle of the frame with his broad back square to the camera from the first frame, the back of his cap, the back of his thick neck and his rounded shoulders in dark gold silk toward the camera, his head facing straight away from the camera toward the trunk of the big old tree at the right; he is the only person in the frame; stung and sulking: his shoulders hunched up stiff, his fists clenched at his sides, his head jutting forward; in front of him, soft, the grassy bank running away to the trunk of the big old tree, and beyond it only dry cracked brown earth in bare furrows reaching to the far hills under a thin low mist; their hands hold only what is described here. No second copy of anyone appears. The picture fixes the place and its light only, never the mood. The portly man stands still for a breath, his shoulders rising; then he flings his right wide sleeve out hard to the side and back with one sharp angry shake that snaps the silk, and strides away from the camera with quick heavy steps along the grassy bank toward the big old tree, his broad back square to the camera the whole shot, his fists clenched at his sides, his stiff shoulders jerking with each step, the back of his cap toward the camera; by the end of the shot he has walked well into the distance in the right third of the frame, smaller against the trunk of the tree, still walking away, and the soft grey-gold dawn light stays unchanged. The camera holds a static shot. One continuous shot. The picture is clean, with no subtitles, captions or text anywhere on screen; a thin white mist lying low over the ground, a clean natural film image. Natural, realistic human motion of a real actor: the weight of his heavy body moves with each angry step, and the gold silk folds and swings over his back and sleeves.

s06.text:
For the target video, <Picture 1>, <Picture 2> and <Picture 3> are referenced throughout.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Photorealistic live-action film footage of real actors in an ancient Chinese (Song-dynasty) period drama, with the look of a feature film. Xu Yan shown in <Picture 1> and <Picture 2> (the same man from several angles) keeps exactly the same face, hair and costume as the pictures: East Asian young man of twenty-five, clean-cut handsome with thick brows, double-lidded bright eyes, straight nose and a firm mouth, tall and lean with broad shoulders, black hair gathered up into a topknot on the crown and tied with a cloth band, a few strands falling over his forehead, a faded blue-grey cotton scholar's robe patched at one elbow, cloth shoes; the earthen brick wall shown in <Picture 3> is the wall of the room, its bricks and its warm light. Initial composition: Inside the farmhouse of the Xu family late at night on the tenth day of the drought, by the small window in the back wall; the one small warm flame on the table the only light, the corners of the room deep in shadow: medium shot by the small window in the earthen brick back wall: the small square window is covered with pale off-white window paper pasted over a plain wooden lattice, the paper blank and smooth, faintly lit on the inside by the warm flame and dark behind it, and in the lower right corner of the window a ragged hole the size of a fist torn through the paper, black night showing through the hole; Xu Yan, in his faded blue-grey scholar's robe patched at one elbow with an old grey cloth outer coat worn loose over his shoulders, dark shadows under his eyes, standing side-on at the window, framed from the waist up, his right hand already holding a balled-up piece of old grey cloth against the torn hole from the first frame, his face turned three-quarter to screen right over his shoulder toward someone out of sight beyond the right edge of the frame, never the lens; that side of the frame is only the earthen brick wall in the warm light of the one small flame all the way to the edge, and he is the only person in the frame; gentle and steady: brows easing, lips moving softly between words, no smile at any moment, not even at the end of the shot, until the last frame; their hands hold only what is described here. No second copy of anyone appears. Facial expressions follow the action and lines described below, not the reference pictures: the pictures fix the face, hair and costume only, never the mood. Xu Yan speaks a short Mandarin line, 「別怕，哥把洞堵上，蝗蟲進不來」, his lips moving evenly with every syllable in small natural talking mouth shapes, no smile at any moment, not even at the end of the shot, until the last frame, his face turned three-quarter to screen right over his shoulder toward someone out of sight beyond the right edge of the frame, his eyes on that spot, never looking at the camera; as he speaks his fingers push the grey cloth into the torn hole bit by bit, the paper around the hole crinkling and giving under his knuckles, until the cloth fills the hole and he presses it flat once with his palm, the rest of the window paper staying whole and blank, and the warm light of the one small flame stays unchanged. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed. One continuous shot. The picture is clean, with no subtitles, captions or text anywhere on screen; the air is clear and still, a clean natural film image. Natural, realistic human motion and acting of real actors: each person keeps the identity, hair and costume of their reference pictures, while every visible face acts the emotion written above and changes with it; the pictures are neutral studio portraits, never copy their blank expression.
